note: The second XPath argument (hex-encoded RC4 ciphertext 'fc8e') is popped from the XPath value stack; its bytes are the origin of the tainted data flow.
The first XPath argument (RC4 key) is popped and later used to derive the key material.
Key is copied into a 128-byte zero-padded buffer (RC4_KEY_LENGTH) which is the actual RC4 key used for decryption.
Hex ciphertext string is decoded into raw binary bytes in bin; ret_len is the resulting byte length of the ciphertext.

code: PLATFORM_RC4_DECRYPT (ctxt, padkey, bin, ret_len, ret, ret_len);
note: RC4 stream decryption writes arbitrary plaintext bytes into ret: ciphertext 'fc8e' under zero-padded key 'x' decrypts to 0xffff, which is not valid UTF-8.

The decrypted bytes are NUL-terminated and treated as an XML string. There is no xmlCheckUTF8 validation before this point, so invalid UTF-8 produced by decryption is never rejected (missing validity check is the root cause).
The raw decrypted string containing invalid UTF-8 is returned to the XPath engine as the function result, exposing invalid UTF-8 in the output of crypto:rc4_decrypt.
